title: In-Phase Quadrature Explorer
description: Three live bar meters for the in-phase component, quadrature component, and combined magnitude, plus a plot of all three across the full phase range showing magnitude invariance.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Correlation
Signals and Systems

educational.topic: In-phase and quadrature components; phase independence
learningObjectives: Examine how I and Q vary with phase
Compare their variation against the invariant magnitude
Explain why a frequency bin must carry two numbers
prerequisites: Sine and cosine differ by a quarter cycle

equations: I = (2/N) sum x[n] sin(2 pi f n / fs)
Q = (2/N) sum x[n] cos(2 pi f n / fs)
assumptions: Signal at 500 Hz with a 128-sample window at 8 kHz, exactly 8 bins
limitations: Off-bin frequencies give a magnitude slightly below 1 due to scalloping loss; this sim sits exactly on a bin to isolate the phase effect

keyQuestions: At what phase does I alone report zero?
Why must a frequency bin carry two numbers?
commonMisconceptions: That a zero correlation against a sine means the frequency is absent
That phase must be known in advance to detect a tone
assessmentOpportunities: Name two situations producing a zero in-phase reading and how to distinguish them
